_comment: What the collector looks for. Edit this file to change the search;
YouTube search is not like a news database. It ignores most boolean
syntax and matches loosely against titles, descriptions and tags, so
these are short plain phrases rather than the long OR-chains the news
crawler uses. Quoted phrases do still get treated as phrases.
Videos are what gets searched. Comments are then pulled from the
videos that look relevant, so a bad video filter wastes nothing but
does bury good comments under junk.
_relevance_comment: A video is scored on its title, channel name and description. Two
points for a topic phrase, one each for an opposition word (up to
two), a named county, a named state, and a local-news channel.
Below keep_threshold its comments are not fetched at all.
_limits_comment: YouTube's developer policies require stored API data to be deleted or
refreshed within 30 calendar days. Every run re-fetches comments for
every tracked video, which keeps them inside that window. max_tracked
is the cap on how many videos stay in the refresh cycle; when a video
drops out, its comment text is removed and only the link and your own
coding remain. Export before that if you need the words.
search.list bills to its own bucket of about 100 calls a day.
commentThreads costs one unit per page of 100 comments from the
10,000-unit pool, so comments are effectively free and searching is
the thing to keep an eye on.
